the development of a scintillator hodo-scope for the COSY- TOF barrel detector, the characterization and optimization of the detector performance, and the implementation of a data acquisition system.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BARREL1 is an excellent detector for the determination of the velocity vectors of charged ejectiles in the angular range Θ =0°–80°.

the BARREL1 is well suited to fulfill the requirements of the COSY–TOF spectrometer for the measurement of the polar angle of the ejectiles and for the time-of-flight measurement of the charged ejectiles.

the new barrel detector is an important component of the TOF spectrometry and has been successfully used for the measurement of the angular and time-of-flight distributions in the reaction pp→dπ+ at 2.5 and 2.9 GeV beam momentum, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BARREL1 scintillator hodo-scope fulfils our requirements for a high precision time-of-flight measurement and a precise determination of the point of impact for charged ejectiles emerging in a large solid angle from the target.
the BARREL1 scintillator hodo- scope fulfils all requirements for the application in a TOF spectrometer.
BARREL1 fulfills all requirements for its application in the COSY- TOF spectrometer and is now in operation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the barrel-shaped scintillators are a viable option for a TOF spectrometer, especially if the angular resolution in the azimuthal direction is not critical.

the barrel-shaped scintillation hodoscope BARREL1 is a very efficient and cost-effective detector for the measurement of the position and time-of-flight of charged particles in high-energy proton–proton reactions.
the barrel hodoscope is a robust and reliable device for the determination of charged particle trajectories in the angular range of 10°–160°.
